precepts.text: Cursed be the day wherein I was born. Jeremiah is saying the same thing Job said. We never celebrated birthdays; that custom came from the nations, from what they dug up in their archaeological digs. It is not of God.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says the same thing Job said: “Cursed be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed.” Two prophets, and neither one blessed the day of his birth. Put that together with Pharaoh's birthday in Genesis 40, where the baker was hanged at the feast.

We never celebrated birthdays. They are days of narcissism, days to put ourselves up above God. The custom came from the nations; it came through the white man, who got it from what they dug up in their archaeological digs, and then taught that we should be celebrating birthdays.

So stop celebrating that foolishness, even with the excuse that it's for the children. Shut up, you narcissist. It is not of God. It's of the devil. And after that birthday feast, “Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.”

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

precepts.why:
“Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name.” That is Jeremiah dismayed at all the work he was set to. Go back to chapter 1 and see: he tried to run away from it, and the Lord did not let him. Most of us are the same; we see the task at hand, but we have not been properly fortified to see how important the mission is.

“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee”. The Lord sent a search party for you; he already knew since the womb what he created. “and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” He hired you to be a prophet.

“Then said I, Ah, Lord God! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.” Lord, this work is too mighty for me; I don't know too much, I'm weak, I ain't nobody. Most of my brothers have that same weak spirit. Shake it off. The little that you know, that you mastered Deuteronomy 28 and smashing John 3:16, the Lord can use; now apply it and let the Lord do his work. Give him something to work with.

“But the Lord said unto me, Say not, I am a child”: stop making excuses. “for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak.” We have to speak it; we are bound by that. “Be not afraid of their faces”: the same thing read in Ezekiel, the same task, the same mission. “for I am with thee to deliver thee, saith the Lord.” That power with us is great, unstoppable. Brothers, gird up your loins, and sisters too.

That is why, when Jeremiah tried to hold back, “his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.” That is the course we are setting: our faces hardened with the word of God. And do not think we get beamed up by chariots and skip Jacob's trouble; our forefathers went through the suffering and we have to go through it too. That is the ticket to the kingdom.

note.label: The Last Man Standing

precepts.why:
This goes with what we read in Ecclesiasticus 18, that giving in to your lust will make you a laughingstock to your enemies that malign you. “For I heard the defaming of many, fear on every side.” Many people try to defame us, on every side. “Report, say they, and we will report it”: tell us the story so that we can say it.

“All my familiars watched for my halting”: your familiars are your friends and family, and halting is falling. “Saying, Peradventure he will be enticed”: hopefully that nigga will give in to his temptation, “and we shall prevail against him, and we shall take our revenge on him”, because he is always correcting us about the Bible, about God's laws, and they hate that. As soon as he falls, they are happy.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

precepts.why:
Jeremiah became sick of the Israelites and said he would not speak any more in the Lord's name. “But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones”. He grew weary of holding it back and could not stay silent.

That is the same burning Cleopas described. You can go to the street saying you will let the brothers teach, then hear somebody's foolishness and feel the scriptures burning until you ask for the microphone. The word moves you to speak even when you planned to hold back.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

precepts.why:
How was he deceived? “Go and take the little book which is open in the hand of the angel.” “Take it, and eat it up; and it shall make thy belly bitter, but it shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey.” When we first heard this word it was sweet. We first heard that we are the Israelites, that Christ only died for us, and could not put the book down; the Bible got wrinkled in the bed because we read until we fell asleep. Our whole world changed.

Then the words started getting bitter. We might die, we might go to jail, we might lose wives, children and friends. We cannot smoke weed, there is no precept for it. If we sneak and do these things, eternal damnation. The word of God constrains us, and at the end we may lose our lives behind this truth. It seems good when you first hear it, then you hear the severity.

The severity: a woman tried to run the brothers over with her car for reading the Bible. Brothers lost their jobs after last week’s blitz when their employers saw it, men with wives, children and mortgages. Every time we go out, our lives are on the line. So in camp, especially in tight quarters, pay attention, get off the phone, and always watch a person’s hands and eyes; they will tell you what he is about to do.

“And I took the little book out of the angel’s hand, and ate it up; and it was in my mouth sweet as honey: and as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter. And he said unto me, Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.” John was on the isle of Patmos, in prison; he already knew the bitterness of the word. He is speaking of this time: we are coming back to do the same thing again, to teach the people whether they hear or forbear, and to be cast into prison, put to death, beaten, and lose homes and jobs. This is the condition of the battle. We will travel the world to preach before nations, tongues and kings.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

precepts.why: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee.” God knew us before he formed us; we were chosen. “And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet.” None of us is here by chance. It is ordained of God that in our time we would be woken up to who we are in the truth. Now that we know it, we have to get ourselves right and go out and find the people and bid them to this wedding. That is why we are on the corners and why we travel the world: to do the work God called us to do. We were ordained to be prophets.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

precepts.why:
“For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.” Appointed to death. Look at these Power Rangers walking the streets in order, they say; they think we are clowns, not knowing they are witnessing the sons of God back on the earth.

“We are fools for Christ’s sake, but ye are wise in Christ; we are weak, but ye are strong.” The people will be made wise and strong in Christ by what we teach. “Ye are honourable, but we are despised.”

“Even unto this present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwellingplace.” These men were ostracized and called fools for teaching this word, lost everything and had no certain dwelling place. “And labour, working with our own hands: being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it.” We hold jobs; we are not sitting here collecting tithes to pay our bills. Their pastors are not on the front line; the only time they come out is to collect money or for a photo op. And people ask why we march instead of helping in Chicago; we have already been there.

“Being defamed, we intreat: we are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day.” We have been called sellouts, witches, pedophiles, wife abusers, gay; we are looked at as the filth of the world.

“I write not these things to shame you, but as my beloved sons I warn you.” Prepare your soul for temptation and tribulation; this is what you signed up for. “For though ye have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet have ye not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel.” Paul was beaten and imprisoned, and says follow the example I set; he asked nothing he had not gone through. We ask the men to go out there, and there is nothing we are not doing or have not done. In Orlando, years ago, there was nowhere to stand, no foot traffic and no reader but a six-year-old son; the word was taught to the buses, the bus stop and the parking lots. The word does not go out void: today Orlando, Miami, Tallahassee, Jacksonville and Tampa are full of Israelites.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

precepts.why: “I am as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright man is laughed to scorn.” They laugh at us. A young brother says he is a virgin and they ask if he is gay. They laugh us to scorn: you are the prophets in that outfit, looking like a Power Ranger, with that beard? You are nobody.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
Purpose is the reason for which something exists or is done, and Jeremiah knew his. “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee”: God knew his soul and his spirit. “And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.”

That was his purpose, and it stayed with him through everything he went through. To realize you have been called to something higher is what turns weariness into praise. Until you have graduated to purpose in this, you are just spending your time here, deciding by emotion and rationalizing after the fact.

Jeremiah went through all of it and realized there is something inside him that will never stop, and if it means he dies doing it, so be it. Purpose conquers weariness. We are going to get the reproach, but face it head on with zeal, trusting that the Most High is always faithful to his laborers.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
A different example of the burning in the heart. “Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?” This is when the disciples saw Christ. He opened their understanding and they saw the prophecies fulfilled in him, and it lit something in them: a yearning, a compulsion, a compassion that moves you.

It is the same burning Jeremiah felt, but Jeremiah’s came through affliction, and this came through understanding and revelation. Jeremiah’s fire was the compulsion to speak truth despite suffering, growing stronger the more he suffered; the disciples’ was awareness and joy at things being revealed. You need both.

Most people have the Luke kind for a season: a class comes out and it was fire. But when the word is truly received, it ignites a purpose for a mission inside you. When your heart burns from the word, your mouth must open to teach it from understanding, and when you go through things it should pull you back to your purpose so you move forward and share it.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
“Who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner’s fire, and like fullers’ soap.” This speaks of Christ, because Christ is the word, the word made flesh. When you ignite that fire you are keeping the spirit of Christ in you, the one who knocks and comes in, in Revelation 3:20.

“He shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver.” The word of fire cleans, refines, purifies, purges, divides and discerns. It consumes because you are convicted.

The real reason many don’t give themselves wholly and don’t want that fire is that having it in your bones is like looking in a mirror and seeing the worst version of yourself, and then having to do something about it. Many would rather cover it with makeup than let the word go into the inward parts and find things out about them. The truth hurts, and the process is painful, but you can’t push it under the rug and expect the fire to do its work halfway. The transformative power of the word fills you with purpose, and this is not even our final form.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
“Behold, the name of the Lord cometh from far, burning with his anger, and the burden thereof is heavy: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire.”

“The burden thereof is heavy” goes into what Jeremiah said when he could not bear it: to have that in you, it has to be put out. As 1 Timothy 4 says, when you truly give yourself wholly you will be saving others without even thinking about it. That is letting your light shine: a city cannot be hid. It takes no conscious effort, but it takes action.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why: “The voice of the Lord divideth the flames of fire.” That is another level of how powerful the word is. Imagine the little droplet of that power we receive from the word, and don’t think it won’t have its cleansing, driving effect, moving you and filling you with purpose even in the face of affliction.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why: “For the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God.” It uses these terms that we may understand. As you build yourself up to the point of wanting that fire, it will test you and purge all things even inside you. It cleanses into obedience and consumes the rebellious spirit. If you are a rebellious brother or sister, let this word in the way it has been built out here, step by step with application. You can’t just say fire, activate; you have to go through the parts.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why: “For our God is a consuming fire.” It says the same thing as Deuteronomy 4:24, reconfirming it: the God whose word burns in Jeremiah’s bones consumes.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
“My heart was hot within me, while I was musing the fire burned: then spake I with my tongue.” To muse is to think upon many things. It happens inside first, in the mind, then into the bones and the spirit, and then it comes out of the mouth.

The musing goes into the meditation scriptures: giving yourself wholly, studying the doctrine, applying. It is the same as Luke 24:32, where their hearts burned within them.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
“There appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.”

This was a miracle, not gibberish. Read on and they were from different countries, each hearing in his own native language, with no translator needed. But the point is that the fire filled them with compulsion to do something. When the word is revealed, the spirit is kindled within, and that produces the passion and drive to speak the word: the utterance.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
“For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit.” When you muse on it and give yourself to it, it finds the wrong and the right. If you are not double minded and submit to it, letting it purge and purify, it activates something in you, and when obstacles come you know where to surrender to overcome them.

“And is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” People say, that wasn’t my intent, as if that makes the action harmless, but the word reveals the intent. It pierces the inward man. It is the fire and the sword, an aggressive process designed to separate truth from error, fact from fiction, sin from what is good and holy.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
“It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” That is how you get the fire, how you quicken and keep your spirit alive, the spiritual man or woman functioning.

The word of God is that fire, but unless you apply everything else from the beginning it won’t do what it needs to do in you. It burns inside so you desire to teach and share, and it devours any resistance against it. Even when the one you taught is not persuaded, it does not invalidate God’s word: they have been touched, either to repent or to be set firmer in their evil. It refines and purifies if you receive it in; it judges, discerns and gives life to the spirit.

That is the fire we all carry. The question is how big: a little ash with some warmth, or the roaring fire seen in how you move. It is not fleshly; it is zeal, the word inside you fully.

He is saying, I was deceived; I thought it was going to be easy, and I learned it is not.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

points: “Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name.” I am catching too much hell; I will not mention this anymore or speak in his name. “But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones.” It was etched into his mind; he could not help it. That is why you cannot turn back now: you have already heard this word. If the spirit of God is in you, it burns in you. Even when you feel you are going through too much, it will eat you alive that you want to do the work, and even though you are afraid, you will do it.

“And I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.” Forbearing is being restrained. He was weary with holding back from teaching; he could not stay, because the word was in him and he could not keep quiet. The door of utterance was given to him, and it was impossible not to teach. That is the spirit we have to have.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

points: “For I heard the defaming of many, fear on every side.” “All my familiars watched for my halting”: all of our people are waiting for us to fall so they can talk. That is why we had better be blameless in this truth; they hope to find some smut to say we are evil. “Saying, Peradventure he will be enticed, and we shall prevail against him, and we shall take our revenge on him.” Perhaps he will be enticed to sin against God, and then they have a reason to mock: look at this hypocrite, that Israelite stuff is BS. Let it not be named among us.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

points: “His word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones.” That is how this Bible needs to be for us: the word burning in our hearts, and not only burning but shut up in the bones. When you feel something deep in your bones it is inescapable. It is not surface level. It is not something we do; it is who we are.
“And I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.” In this moment Jeremiah felt like giving up, but the word always wins, and it would not let him give up.

Brothers and sisters talk about being tired and weary, and brothers misuse battle fatigue. The Bishop taught battle fatigue and it went over everybody’s head: battle fatigue really means sin is winning, your flesh beating you up so you don’t want to keep these laws anymore. Most of the men who say they are battle fatigued are just lazy. No passion, no fire. That is why all the excuses abound.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: Up to this point Jeremiah had been warning of the judgment of the Most High and blasting Judah for their treachery and corruption. Everybody wants to blame the northern kingdom, as if the southern kingdom did not do the same or worse. Judah saw what happened to the northern kingdom and still did it, which makes them worse, because they knew better.

“Now Pashur the son of Immer the priest, who was also chief governor in the house of the Lord, heard that Jeremiah prophesied these things”: the wars and the judgment that Jeremiah prophesied against their wickedness.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “Then Pashur smote Jeremiah the prophet”: he beat him up, just for prophesying the truth, “and put him in the stocks that were in the high gate of Benjamin, which was by the house of the Lord.”

The stocks held him twisted up with his head locked in, and they were set in a public place so that everybody could shame him: throwing things at him, cursing him, spitting on him, and he could do nothing. That is done to break a man’s spirit. Examine yourself: is anything you are dealing with strong enough to break your spirit and fire for the Lord? The answer should be unequivocally hell no.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “The Lord hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magor–missabib.” Magor–missabib means fear round about, which is why he says “I will make thee a terror to thyself.” The stocks did not break Jeremiah’s spirit. He came out emboldened and cursed him.

Jeremiah had no power to “give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon.” That is the spirit of the Lord speaking through him: Pashur, his house and all his friends to whom he had prophesied lies would go into captivity and die in Babylon, and Judah with them.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: Verses 7 onward show where Jeremiah’s spirit was while he was locked up in the stocks, communing with the Lord.

“O Lord, thou hast deceived me, and I was deceived.” He is not saying God lied to him. He did not realize how powerful his calling would be: that after being beaten and put in the stocks he would come out wanting to preach the word all the more. It is like the apostles who rejoiced when they came out of prison because they had been afflicted for Christ’s name, and it made them more zealous. That is a unique spirit, and not everybody has it.
“Thou art stronger than I, and hast prevailed.” He was ready to give up and considered it in his mind, but the fire the Lord put in him took him to another level.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “For since I spake, I cried out, I cried violence and spoil”: what he prophesied against Judah. “Because the word of the Lord was made a reproach unto me, and a derision, daily.” Every time he spoke the word he was cursed out, spit on, beaten, chased out of town and thrown in the stocks.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name.” He considered not prophesying anymore, like brothers and sisters who say they have to get right before they come back, as if you can get right without the word.

“But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones.” Verse 7 is explained in verse 9: he was deceived because he did not realize how powerful the word was in him. The spirit is stronger than the flesh.

“I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay”: weary of trying not to do the Lord’s will. He does not mean he wanted to give up; he means, I am tired of fighting you, God; you are stronger than me. Something is shut up inside him, and the spirit will not let him rest until he speaks. If you have never felt that, where you have to say something to rebuke and correct a spirit and bring the edification out, you are not where you need to be yet in this walk.

Compulsion is a strong, usually irresistible impulse to perform an act, especially one contrary to one’s will. In the flesh Jeremiah had every right to give up, but that compulsion would not let him. The fire conquers weariness. With it you will never have battle fatigue and never think of walking away, even when people you love walk away. Your salvation is not tied to anybody else; it is built on this word and on Christ.
If his word is truly in your heart, it will burn until you speak it. There is never a time when there is nothing to talk about in the scriptures; it should always be a discovery.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “I heard the defaming of many, fear on every side.” “All my familiars watched for my halting, saying, Peradventure he will be enticed, and we shall prevail against him, and we shall take our revenge on him.” These are the things he was dealing with.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “But the Lord is with me as a mighty terrible one: therefore my persecutors shall stumble, and they shall not prevail.” Here he explains what he reasoned out in the stocks. He is encouraging himself, building himself up, feeding the fire he has from the Lord. “For unto thee have I opened my cause.”

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: “Sing unto the Lord, praise ye the Lord: for he hath delivered the soul of the poor from the hand of evildoers.” His struggle turns to praise because he realizes his purpose. Knowing there is a God and that redemption waits on the other side, whatever you are afflicted with, is what built him up.

This is the cost of conviction. For some of us it will literally happen again; you see shades of it in the travels and in how people attack us. That inescapable drive makes you run toward danger, like the man who runs into a burning building to save someone, and that is compassion again. It shows you are a real one, a true servant, not a fair-weather friend who stops being a friend in times of difficulty. Imagine having to gather in secret upon pain of death like our forefathers, when some cannot even make it in when they are depressed.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

points: Still dealing with fire, tying all the fire together. “His word was in mine heart as a burning fire”: you can’t keep it in; it has to be spoken. “Shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.” I have to preach this word. The word ignites an inward compulsion so that you cannot remain silent.
